chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-'Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

If you are in a situation where you cannot manage anything except clay, then perform tayammum with it, for Allah, Exalted is He, is more deserving of accepting the excuse, when you do not have with you a dry garment nor felt that you are able to shake off and perform tayammum with.

key_terms.الطِّينِ: clay, the only available substance for tayammum in this case
key_terms.الْعُذْرِ: excuse, the state of constraint recognized in the ruling
key_terms.ثَوْبٌ جَافٌّ: a dry garment that could serve as a source of dust for tayammum
key_terms.فَتَيَمَّمْ: perform tayammum, the dry ablution prescribed here
key_terms.لِبْدٌ: felt or a thick fabric that may be shaken to obtain dust for tayammum

ai.seo_question: Can tayammum be performed with clay when no dry earth or cloth is available?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for tayammum in a constrained situation where only clay is available. It indicates that one may perform tayammum with clay when no dry material such as a dry cloth or felt is available to use instead, recognizing the excuse in such necessity.
